text:
VAN had about a one-in-ten chance of winning this game on the quality of its chances, and it spent most of the night proving the odds right until the clock stopped. VGK finished with 4.49 expected goals to VAN's 1.51 and 60 shot attempts to 36, yet it took a goal 34 seconds after a VAN equalizer to settle a 3-2 result at Rogers Arena. Kevin Lankinen made it closer than it should have been, saving 1.49 goals more than the 28 shots he faced deserved.

VAN scored first when Paul Cotter tipped in a power-play goal at 18:52 of the first, an 11% chance, even though VGK led that period 1.73 to 0.67 in expected goals. The second period was the real gap: VGK out-chanced VAN 2.14 to 0.54. Mitch Marner tied it at 9:01, and Victor Olofsson put VGK ahead on the power play at 14:30. Olofsson was on the ice for 2.28 expected goals for and 0.18 against in 14:36.

Then came the oddity. Jonathan Lekkerimäki tied it at 17:54 on a 5% chance, the least likely goal of the night. Marc Gatcomb answered at 18:28, a 31% look assisted by Braeden Bowman and Nic Dowd, and that was the winner. VGK went 1 for 5 on the power play despite 1.68 expected goals, while VAN's 1 for 3 came off just 0.21. VAN blocked 20 shots to VGK's 7, which helps explain how a game this lopsided stayed within reach.
